evidence: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/comparison/ComparisonUrlHandler.tsx:47 — `return response.json() as Promise<ListingSummary>;` casts the raw fetch body of GET /api/v1/listings/{id} straight to ListingSummary with no runtime shape validation, then feeds it into addToComparison() (comparison-context.tsx:71) and the comparison UI.

Inconsistent with the SSR detail page for the SAME endpoint: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/listings/[slug]/page.tsx:79-89 only does `if (!response.ok) return null` then routes the body through `parseListingDetail(body)` precisely because (per its own inline comment, lines 80-87) a 200 response can carry a malformed/partial body (missing nested fields, wrong-typed `features`/`photos`) that crashes render. ComparisonUrlHandler guards response.ok (line 44) but performs no equivalent body normalization/validation.

Impact: a malformed/partial 200 body for a shared-comparison id (?ids=... deep link on the public /compare page) flows unvalidated into the comparison view and can crash client rendering. No parseListingSummary normalizer exists in src/lib — the parse pattern is applied to detail bodies but not summary bodies. Fix: add/apply a parseListingSummary normalizer (mirroring parseListingDetail) and drop the raw `as Promise<ListingSummary>` cast, dropping ids whose body fails validation (the loop already degrades gracefully via Promise.allSettled).
